newsitem.title: USA: Law firm says it sues Advanta Corp.
newsitem.headline: Law firm says it sues Advanta Corp.

text.p: Advanta Corp was hit with a law suit requesting class action status filed by those who bought Advanta shares between August 13, 1996 through March 17, 1997, lawyers for the plaintiffs said Tuesday.
Advanta allegedly announced earnings news which failed to disclose the fact that the performance of its credit card operations had reversed course, a news release issued by the lawyers said.
The suit was filed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, according to the law firms of Bernard Gross PC and Stull Stull & Brody.
The company allegedly changed its accounting method to hide the trend reversal, the news release said.
An Advanta spokeswoman could not be reached for comment.

The complaint alleges that while the problems were concealed from the public, during the class period certain officers and directors sold over 890,000 shares of Advanta common stock for proceeds of over $39 million, the news release said.

Plaintiffs claim that when accurate information became known, the price of Advanta common stock declined over 20 percent to $31.875 per share, causing substantial losses for Advanta investors during the class period, the news release said.
